title: Developer experience docs: SDK guides, quickstarts, templates, API examples, and docs-site operating procedures
author: Priya Kapoor
body:
Summary
------
This playbook standardizes how Developer Experience (DevEx) produces and maintains SDK guides, quickstarts, templates, and API examples, and it codifies docs-site operating procedures and the canonical fixes for the top support issues. The goal is to reduce friction for product and platform teams shipping API and SDK changes while improving self-serve success for external and internal users.

Scope and audience
------------------
- Scope: SDK reference guides, language quickstarts, code templates, API request/response examples, docs-site publishing and review workflow, and canonical support fixes.
- Audience: SDK authors, technical writers, Solutions Engineers, Support Engineers, and Docs reviewers.

Principles
----------
1. Accuracy first: examples must be runnable and pass CI smoke tests.
2. Minimal friction: quickstarts should get a developer from zero to first successful API call in <= 5 minutes.
3. Reproducibility: include pinned SDK versions and example credentials placeholders.
4. Observability: every doc must include owner, last-updated date, and links to related routes and telemetry dashboards.

Roles and ownership
------------------
- Author: owns initial content and example code.
- Reviewer: at least one SDK engineer + one tech writer.
- Docs owner (DevEx): triages doc bugs and coordinates publishing (team: eng-developer-experience).
- Support escalation: Customer Success for account-specific issues, Engineering for platform/SDK bugs.

File and metadata standards
-------------------------
- Filenames: short, descriptive, kebab-case, include year when stable (e.g., developer-experience-sdk-quickstarts-2027.json).
- Required metadata fields (in page JSON): title, space, author, owner_team, status, created_at, last_updated.
- Optional metadata: reviewers, labels (0–8), related_pages, confidentiality.
- Content must be plain text/Markdown-style with clear sections.

SDK Guide template (canonical sections)
-------------------------------------
1. Title & one-line summary
2. Audience and prerequisites (SDK version, API access key, required permissions)
3. Quickstart (code snippet that runs end-to-end)
4. API reference (endpoint, method, required params, example request & response)
5. Common pitfalls & debugging tips
6. Testing & CI integration (how to run the snippet in CI)
7. Changelog & compatibility notes
8. Owner and contact info

Example SDK Quickstart (Python)
-------------------------------
Prereqs: Python 3.10+, pip install redwood-inference-sdk==1.12.0

# Example (Python)
from redwood_inference import Client
client = Client(api_key="<REDWOOD_API_KEY>")
resp = client.generate(model="open-llama-13b", prompt="Say hello from Redwood!", max_tokens=50)
print(resp.text)

- Note: use environment variables for keys in CI. Provide a minimal Dockerfile in the template subdirectory for reproducibility.

Node quickstart (curl + JS)
---------------------------
- curl example for quick verification:
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY' 
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
    -d '{"model":"open-llama-13b","prompt":"Hello from Redwood!","max_tokens":32}'

- NodeJS snippet should mirror the SDK: require('@redwood/inference').Client and async/await example.

API Examples and Response Contracts
----------------------------------
Each API example must include: endpoint, HTTP method, minimum required headers, sample JSON body, and a canonical response example. Include both success and common error responses.

Sample API example (JSON)
Request:
POST /v1/generate
Headers:
- Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>
- Content-Type: application/json
Body:
{
  "model": "open-llama-13b",
  "input": "Summarize the following text...",
  "max_tokens": 150
}
Response (200):
{
  "id": "gen_abc123",
  "model": "open-llama-13b",
  "output": "...summary...",
  "usage": {"prompt_tokens": 45, "completion_tokens": 55, "total_tokens": 100}
}

Docs-site operating procedures (publishing flow)
----------------------------------------------
1. Author creates content branch in docs repo (docs/ or content/ depending on site). Include JSON metadata file matching Confluence schema.
2. Add runnable examples and a smoke test for the quickstart in tests/integration/.
3. Open PR against main, include the following PR checklist:
   - [ ] Metadata present and valid
   - [ ] Quickstart runnable locally and in CI
   - [ ] Reviewers assigned: SDK eng + tech writer
   - [ ] Labels added: language tags + doc-type
4. CI runs doc-lint and example smoke tests. PR cannot be merged until green.
5. Reviewer(s) approve → docs owner schedules publish window.
6. Post-publish: update change log section and ping #docs-updates Slack channel.

Review and update cadence
------------------------
- Quickstarts: review every 6 months or on SDK major releases.
- API examples: review on every API change (PR must reference related API ADR).
- Deprecated examples: annotate with deprecation date and recommended replacement; remove after 12 months.

Top support issues and canonical fixes (current priority)
------------------------------------------------------
1) Authentication failures (most common)
   - Symptom: 401 or 403 responses when using examples.
   - Root causes: using expired API key, missing Authorization header, wrong environment (staging vs prod).
   - Canonical fix steps:
     1. Confirm API key in environment: echo $REDWOOD_API_KEY (do not paste value in tickets).
     2. Verify header format: Authorization: Bearer <KEY>.
     3. Check account permissions if 403; escalate to Customer Success with request id and timestamp.

2) Mismatched SDK version causing breaking examples
   - Symptom: runtime errors or missing methods.
   - Root causes: examples pinned to out-of-date SDK or developer using latest SDK with breaking changes.
   - Canonical fix steps:
     1. Confirm SDK version: pip show redwood-inference or npm ls @redwood/inference.
     2. Update example to include version pin or add compatibility note.
     3. If regression, create SDK issue and link the doc PR to the issue.

3) Streaming responses not handled by example code
   - Symptom: example waits until timeout or prints incomplete chunks.
   - Root causes: example uses non-streaming client or lacks event handlers.
   - Canonical fix steps:
     1. Replace synchronous example with streaming handler (code snippet included in fix template).
     2. Add test that verifies chunked output is received and stitched.

4) Token accounting confusion (unexpected billing)
   - Symptom: users report higher token counts than expected.
   - Root causes: mismatch between prompt formatting, hidden system messages, or wrong usage metrics interpretation.
   - Canonical fix steps:
     1. Add a token accounting section to the quickstart showing how to compute prompt vs completion tokens.
     2. Provide example that prints usage object from the response and explains each field.

Canonical fixes repository and templates
--------------------------------------
- All canonical fixes live in confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/canonical-fixes/ as separate pages named for the issue (auth-failures-fix-2027.json).
- Each fix page includes: symptom, steps (numbered), example commands, related logs/diagnostics to collect, and escalation contact.

Quality gates and CI checks for examples
-------------------------------------
- Doc-lint: checks headings, metadata, forbidden words (no secrets), and labels.
- Example-smoke: runs quickstarts in ephemeral test account with a gated test key.
- Link-checker: validates external links once per week on main branch.

Search and discoverability guidelines
-----------------------------------
- Use 3–7 short, high-signal labels.
- Add a one-line excerpt to metadata used for search snippets.
- Every quickstart must include a "Getting started" H2 within the first 120 words.

Operational metrics (doc health)
------------------------------
- Pageviews (90d)
- Time to first successful API call (from feedback or telemetry)
- Support tickets referencing page (30d)
- Search no-results rate for key terms (query-level)
- CI example pass rate

Maintenance checklist for authors
--------------------------------
- [ ] Run smoke tests locally after SDK/API upgrades
- [ ] Validate examples with the latest CI test key
- [ ] Update "last_updated" metadata on every change
- [ ] Tag reviewers and add changelog entry

Appendix: Useful snippets and templates
------------------------------------
- Dockerfile template: a minimal Dockerfile that installs Python SDK and runs the quickstart smoke test.
- CI job snippet (GitHub Actions): small workflow that runs example-smoke and doc-lint.
- Example issue template for documenting breaking SDK changes and linking affected docs.
